# Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta (MN 139 (PTS MN iii 230))

**ID:** MN 139 (PTS MN iii 230)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Analysis of No Strife
**PTS:** MN iii 230
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

A full parallel is preserved in the Chinese *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 169, *Kurūsvaraṇā Sūtra*) and among Sanskrit manuscript fragments (SHT sutta13) [Huifeng 2012]. Unlike MN 139, MĀ 169 contains material praising the elder Subhūti as the foremost dweller in non-conflict (*araṇavihārin*) and explicitly links *araṇā* to emptiness (*śūnyatā*) [Huifeng 2012].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: MA 169 拘樓瘦無諍; SHT Sutta 13
- Passage-level parallels: MN 122 (PTS MN iii 109) Mahāsuññata Sutta
- Resembling parallels: MN 13 (PTS MN i 83) Mahādukkhakkhandha Sutta; MN 14 (PTS MN i 91) Cūḷadukkhakkhandha Sutta; SN 36.20 Bhikkhusutta; SN 36.19 Pañcakaṅgasutta; AN 6.63 Nibbedhikasutta

**Sources**

- [Norman 1997] K. R. Norman, A Philological Approach to Buddhism (1997) — Structural outline of the sutta as a canonical commentary defining araṇa
- [Dhammapala et al. 1984] Gatare Dhammapala, Richard Gombrich, K. R. Norman (eds.), Buddhist Studies in Honour of Hammalava Saddhatissa (1984) — The Buddha's teachings on provincial dialects and language conventions
- [Winternitz 1933] Maurice Winternitz, A History of Indian Literature, Vol. II (1933) — Contextualization of the sutta's rule on provincial dialects
- [Freyre Roach 2014] Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach, Buddhist and Wittgensteinian Approaches Toward Language (2014) — Analysis of non-conflict and the avoidance of linguistic extremes
- [Eifring 2014] Halvor Eifring (ed.), Hindu, Buddhist and Daoist Meditation: Cultural Histories (2014) — Citation of MN iii 233 on sensual pleasure versus noble happiness
- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha (2003) — Commentarial gloss of raṇa as defilement (raja-kilesa)
- [Huifeng 2012] Shi Huifeng (M. B. Orsborn), Chiasmus in Early Prajñāpāramitā (2012) — Comparison with MĀ 169 and the connection to Subhūti and śūnyatā
